description: A radar chart that changes its scale with every filter makes a 57 look like a 100. Two suppliers that score 3 and 4 out of 5 look like 1 and 5 when the axis starts where the data does. And an empty answer drawn as zero invents a bad score. Radar & Spider Chart by TCViz compares several profiles on several criteria at once — suppliers, employees, products, teams — on a scale that does not move. Power BI has no built-in radar chart; this one starts at zero, keeps your axes in place and draws a gap where a value is missing. READ IT HONESTLY • A common scale from zero, with a minimum and maximum you can fix (1 to 5, 0 to 100) • Axes keep their order when you filter: the order of the field (Sort by column), by name or by value • Empty values drawn as a gap in the outline, never as zero; negative values with the zero ring marked • A note names the axis that flattens the others, and counts values outside a fixed scale • Measures as axes: survey data in columns works without unpivoting PRO • 4 to 12 series (the free version draws 3) • A target per axis, drawn dashed, with the gap on every axis in green or red • A scale per axis, from the data or from minimum and maximum measures, each axis labelling its own rings • "Lower is better" axes, reversed and marked, and a % of target scale • Bands, a reference ring, small multiples or one radar per series on a shared scale • Axis groups…
